exits.label: ◂ back along the water to the Reed-Walk

npcs.name: Odell
npcs.title: an old soul waiting, with great confidence, for a cat
npcs.hail: *(An old man sits in a battered chair at the edge of the grey water, one hand resting palm-up on his knee in the unmistakable, patient posture of a person holding a place for someone to sit — or, you realize, for something to climb into. He is not sad. He is watchful, and a little proud, in the way of a man who has decided to be certain about a thing he is not certain of at all.)* …*(he doesn't look up; he's watching the middle distance)* …you can *sit*, if you *mind* the *lap.* …*(a beat)* …*no* — not *your* *lap. this* one. *(he pats his knee)* …it's *spoken* *for.* …*(now he glances at you, sizing you up)* …you're the *cold* one. the *Returned.* …*good*, then you'll *understand* — you *cross*, you see *things* the *rest* don't. …*(he settles back, confident, the confidence a size too big for him)* …i'm *waiting* on my *cat.* …*Marmalade.* …*she'll* *come.* …*(a fraction less certain)* …she *always* *comes.* …*(the smallest crack)* …*eventually.* …*(and then the bravado, restored)* …*on* her *own* *time*, mind. she's a *cat.* you don't *summon* a cat. …you just …*keep* the *lap* *warm* …and *wait.*

variants.text: *(He clocks the brown dog that trots at your heel — the one that hears the Wall's song, the one that chose you — and his weathered face does something complicated and fond.)* …*(he eyes the dog)* …ah. you've a *dog.* …*(the dog looks at him; he looks at the dog; an ancient species-truce is silently negotiated and declined)* …*hm.* …a *fine* *animal*, i'm *sure.* *loyal.* *comes* when *called.* *wags.* …*(a dry sniff)* …*Marmalade* wouldn't be *caught* *dead* — *(he stops, considers the phrase, we-are-all-dead-here)* …well. …*she* wouldn't come when *called* if the *whole* *grey* was on *fire* and i had a *fish.* …*(and then, quietly, the love under the pride)* …*that's* how you *know* it's *real*, cold one. a *dog* comes for *anyone* with a *kind* *voice.* …a *cat* that comes for *you* …*chose* you. *specifically.* out of *spite* for every *other* option. …*(he pats the waiting lap)* …*sit*, dog-and-all. …but *she* gets the *knee.*

*(His watchful eyes find the cold in you, and the pride softens into something kinder, one waiting soul recognizing another.)* …*(gently)* …you've the *look* of a soul that's *forgotten* what *warm* *feels* *like.* …i *know* that *look.* i *wore* it, before — *(he pats the waiting lap)* …*before* i remembered i was *waiting* on a *warm* thing, and that the *waiting* itself keeps a *body* *warmer* than you'd *think.* …*(he studies you)* …you go from *soul* to *soul*, don't you, cold one. *carrying* things. *never* *stopping.* …*(he nods at the empty chair beside his)* …a soul that *never* *stops* …forgets that *warmth* isn't a thing you *find.* it's a thing you *wait* for, and *keep* a *lap* *ready* for, and *let* *climb* into you when it *deigns* to. …*sit* a while. …*mine's* *late*, and the *company'd* be *welcome.*

*(He watches the grey water and the middle distance, palm up, patient, a man keeping a promise to something that hasn't arrived.)* …*(conversational, unhurried)* …*seventeen* *years* i *had* her, cold one. in the *living* *world.* *Marmalade.* found her in a *woodpile*, half-*drowned* and *furious* about it, *hissing* at the *hand* that *saved* her. …*(fond)* …*never* *did* *thank* me. not *once* in *seventeen* *years.* just …*decided* i was *hers*, and *ruled* me *accordingly.* …*(he pats the lap)* …i *died* *first.* …*(a beat)* …she'd be — she'd have *come* *along* *after*, by *now*, in the *natural* *way* of *things.* *old* *cat.* …so i've been *here.* at the *edge* where the *new* ones *arrive.* …*waiting.* …*keeping* the *lap* *warm.* …*(the certainty thins, just at the edges)* …she'll *know* it's *mine.* …*a* *cat* always *knows* …*whose* *lap* …*(quietly)* …*whose* *lap* is *hers.*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He keeps his palm up, his eyes on the arriving-place, and talks the way lonely people talk when someone finally sits — too much, and gratefully.)* …everyone *tells* me to *stop.* …the other *souls.* '*Odell*, it's been *how* *long*, *Odell*, a *cat* won't — the *grey's* too *wide*, *Odell*, she'll never *find* — ' …*(he waves a gnarled hand)* …*bosh.* …they don't *understand* *cats.* a *dog* you'd *worry* for — a *dog* *panics*, a *dog* *searches*, a *dog* *breaks* its *heart* *looking.* …but a *cat* doesn't *look.* a *cat* *knows* *exactly* where it's *going* and *takes* its *sweet* *time* *getting* there to *punish* you for *making* it *come* at *all.* …*(he almost smiles)* …*Marmalade* isn't *lost*, cold one. …*Marmalade* is *late.* …*on* *purpose.* …*because* she's *furious* i *died* *first* and *left* her, and she's going to make me *WAIT* for it, and when she *finally* *deigns* to *climb* *up* …*(his voice catches, just slightly)* …she'll *pretend* she wasn't *looking* for me at *all.* …*that's* — *(barely)* …*that's* how i'll *know* it's *really* *her.*

choices.text: *(read the old man and his patient, prideful, frightened hope)* "Let me look at you a moment, Odell. Past the confidence. At what the waiting's really made of."

*(the one who crosses, whom the beasts of the grey favor)* "Here's a thing you might not know about me, Odell. I'm the soul the Wall gave back — and the animals of the grey favor me. Dogs follow me. The dead beasts trust the cold that walks both ways. If Marmalade is anywhere on this side, I have a better chance of finding her than any soul here. Let me look for her."
*(go find the cat — the Returned can perceive the animal-souls that drift the grey)* "Keep the lap warm, Odell. I'm going to go and find your cat."
"How long, Odell? Truly. How long have you kept the lap warm?"
"She'll come, Odell. You're right about cats. Keep waiting."
"Rest a while, Odell. I'll be back this way."

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He lets you look, still watching the middle distance, and your sense moves past the practiced bravado about cats to the soul keeping the lap warm.)* *(And you find, first, that he genuinely believes she will come — this is not denial, or not only; a man who lived seventeen years at the mercy of one small furious animal has learned, in his marrow, that the thing does turn up, on its own terms, when least summoned and most wanted, and he is betting his whole afterlife on that pattern holding past death. But your sense reads the fear the confidence is built to cover, and it is not that she won't come. It is subtler and worse: that she will come, and that he will not be here when she does — that he is himself fading, slow, at the grey water's edge, and that his one terror is not the Wall or the dissolving but the arithmetic of it, that if he thins away before she arrives, then the cat he loved will come at last to a warm lap that isn't there, and wait, the way he is waiting now, alone, for a person who cannot come — and that he would endure any eternity to spare her that, to simply be here, solid, palm-up, when she finally deigns. And your sense reads the deepest thing, the reason the waiting is not sad the way you expected: that seventeen years of being chosen by a creature that chooses no one taught this plain old man that he was worth choosing, and that the lap he keeps warm is not really for the cat's comfort but a monument to the one unarguable fact of his life — that something proud and free and impossible to command looked at all its options and picked him, on purpose, out of spite for the world, and stayed. He is not waiting for a pet. He is waiting for the proof that he mattered, and he cannot bear for it to arrive and find him gone.)*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He turns fully toward you for the first time, and the careful pride wavers.)* …the *animals* *favor* you. …*(he searches your cold face)* …*(and then, because he has been brave and certain and alone for so long, the certainty cracks all the way and the fear underneath shows plain)* …would you — *(his voice is not steady now)* …*could* you, cold one? *look* for her? …*(a gnarled hand grips the chair-arm)* …i tell them all she'll *come*, and i *believe* it, i *do* — but the *grey's* so *wide*, and i'm — *(he can't quite say* fading*)* …i'm not as *solid* as i *was*, and i keep *thinking* — what if she *comes* and i've gone *thin* and she *can't* — what if she arrives to an *empty* *chair* and *waits* the way *i've* — …*(he stops, mortified at the crack in him)* …*Marmalade.* orange. a *torn* *ear* — the *left* — she got it in a *fight* she *started.* answers to *nothing*, but she *knows* her *name.* …*(barely)* …*find* her, cold one. …*bring* her *home* to the *lap* …*before* the *lap* …*goes* *cold.*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(You go out into the wide grey where the animal-souls drift — the dead beasts no god ever claimed, waiting or wandering — and your dead-touched sense, the one the animals trust, finds her: an orange cat with a torn left ear, sitting on a grey stone with her tail curled round her feet, looking in precisely the wrong direction with the studied unconcern of a creature who has known exactly where she was going the entire time. You do not carry her. No one carries Marmalade. You simply say Odell's name, once, and walk, and after a long insulting pause she gets up and follows, three steps behind, pretending to be going the same way by coincidence.)* …*(and Odell sees her)* …*(he does not leap up; he knows better; he simply turns his palm up on his knee and goes very still, and waits, the way he has waited an eternity, one breath more)* …*(and Marmalade crosses the last of the grey with magnificent unhurry, and looks at the lap, and looks away, and looks back, and then — as if it were entirely her own idea and nothing to do with him at all — flows up into his lap, turns twice, and settles, purring like a small furious engine, refusing to meet his eye)* …*(Odell's face, cold one. you will carry Odell's face a long way down the road.)* …*(barely, to the cat, not to you)* …*there* you are. …*took* your *time.* …*(and one weathered hand comes down on the orange fur, and stays, and the old man closes his eyes, and the lap is warm, and it was worth every year of the waiting.)*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(You go out into the grey to find her — and you don't have to go far, because she is already coming. Your sense finds Marmalade a hundred yards from the chair and closing, unhurried, deliberate, on a course she plotted the moment she arrived in the dead lands and has been walking, at her own insulting pace, ever since. She was always coming. Odell was right, about the cat and about everything. You didn't find her. You just happened to be there for the last hundred yards of a journey seventeen years and one death in the making.)* …*(you walk beside her, three steps back, at the distance she permits, and Odell looks up, and sees her, and makes the smallest sound)* …*(and Marmalade does not run — cats do not run, it would concede that the destination mattered — she simply arrives, as if she'd meant to all along, as if no time had passed, as if a lap were a lap and this one merely happened to be hers, and pours herself up into it and settles and shuts her eyes and purrs, furious and home)* …*(Odell is weeping, silently, one hand on the orange fur, and he looks at you over the cat's head)* …*'she* *always* *comes,'* he says, and his voice breaks on the *pride* of being *right.* …*'i* *told* them. …*i* *told* them all. …a *cat* that's *yours* …*always* …*comes.'* …*(and the two of them sit at the water's edge, the man and the impossible chosen thing, and face whatever's next together, and the lap is warm, and it will stay warm now, right to the end.)*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(You go out into the wide grey and you look — truly look, everywhere the animal-souls drift — and you cannot find her. The grey is vast, and an orange cat with a torn ear is a very small thing in it, and after a long searching you come back to the chair with empty hands and a heavy heart, and you have to tell Odell you couldn't.)* …*(he takes it better than you feared; he only nods, and keeps his palm up)* …*(gently, forgiving you)* …*'course* you *couldn't.* …you don't *find* a *cat*, cold one. i *told* you that. …*(he pats the lap)* …you don't *find* her. …you *keep* the *lap* *warm* …and *she* *finds* *you.* …*(he settles back, patient, undimmed by your failure)* …*thank* you for *going.* …*most* wouldn't have. …*(a small, certain smile at the middle distance)* …she'll *come.* …you'll *see.* …*come* *back* this *way* …and i'll *wager* you a *year* …there's a *warm* *orange* *weight* …right *here* …where the *lap* is.

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(You didn't find her. Of course you didn't. But as you stand there at the water's edge, having failed, apologizing, there is a sound — the softest possible sound, a small proprietary complaint from somewhere behind the chair — and an orange cat with a torn left ear strolls out of the grey exactly as if it had been there the whole time and you were all being very silly, and regards the two of you with withering unconcern, and then, having made her point, flows up into the waiting lap without a backward glance.)* …*(Odell doesn't say I-told-you-so. He is far too busy. His whole weathered face has come undone around the purring orange weight, and one hand is buried in the fur, and he is not looking at you at all, he is looking at the one creature in all of creation that chose him.)* …*(after a while, without looking up)* …*you* *see*, cold one? …*(thick with tears and triumph)* …you went *looking.* …*bless* you for it. …but a *cat* *isn't* *found.* …a *cat* *arrives* …when *she's* *good* and *ready* …and *not* one *second* *before* …and *always* — *(his voice breaks)* …*always* to the *lap* …that *kept* *itself* *warm* …*for* *her.* …*(and Marmalade purrs, and the old man weeps into her fur, and the wide grey water goes on, and it does not matter, because the waiting is over and the lap is warm and something proud and free came home.)*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He answers without taking his eyes off the arriving-place, and the number, when it comes, is quiet.)* …*how* *long.* …*(a slow breath)* …i've *stopped* *counting*, cold one, because the *counting* was the *only* thing that *frightened* me. …*(he pats the lap)* …*long* *enough* that the *other* *souls* *pity* me. *long* enough that i've *watched* *whole* *souls* *arrive* and *fade* while i've *sat* *here.* …*long* enough that some *mornings* — if there *are* *mornings* — i *wonder* if she — *(he stops the thought, firmly)* …*no.* …*(he sets his jaw)* …*here's* what i *know*, and i'll *stake* my *fading* on it: …*seventeen* *years* she *chose* me, *every* *day*, out of a *world* *full* of *warmer* *laps* and *kinder* *hands.* a *creature* that chooses *no* one *chose* *me.* …*(quietly, certain)* …a *love* like *that* doesn't *get* *lost* in a *bit* of *grey.* …it *takes* its *time.* …it makes you *WAIT.* …*because* it *can.* …*but* it *comes.* …*(he pats the lap)* …*seventeen* *years* taught me to *wait* on *Marmalade.* …*death's* just …a *longer* *evening.* …*she'll* *come* *in* …when the *hunting's* *done.*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He looks at you with unexpected sharpness, then softens, then — for the first time — lets the pride down entirely.)* …*(quietly)* …you're the *first* one, cold one. …*(he shakes his head)* …in *all* this *waiting* …*everyone* who *stops* by *tells* me to *give* *up.* *kindly*, *most* of them. '*let* her *go*, *Odell*, *make* your *peace*, *drift* on.' …*(his voice roughens)* …*you're* the *first* to *sit* down and say *she'll* *come.* …*(he has to look away, at the water)* …you don't *know* what that — a *man* can *wait* *forever* on a *thing* he *believes* in. …but it's *lonely* *work*, *believing* *alone.* …*(he pats the lap, steadier now)* …*thank* you. …for *waiting* *with* me. even a *moment.* …*(the certainty, restored and warmed)* …*now* *go* on, cold one — *before* she *comes* and finds a *stranger* in *her* *spot* and *sulks* *another* *year* out of *spite.* …*(a real smile)* …*come* *back.* …i've a *feeling* …you'll *find* a *warm* *orange* *weight* …*here* …when you *do.*

nodes.speaker: Odell
nodes.text: *(He nods, palm up, eyes on the middle distance, entirely unbothered by your going.)* …*aye.* *go* on. …*(he settles into the chair, patient as stone)* …*i'm* not going *anywhere.* …*(the ghost of a smile)* …*someone* has to *keep* the *lap* *warm.* …*(and as you turn, softly, to himself as much as to you)* …*any* *minute* *now.* …*that's* the *thing* about a *cat*, cold one. …it's *always* …*any* *minute* *now.* …*(and he waits, and there is more peace in his waiting than in half the finished souls you've met, because his is a waiting with a warm certainty at the end of it, and he would not trade it for all the rest in the grey.)*
